user.title: Signal K
user.description: Connect to a Signal K server.

notifications.title: Signal K Notifications
notifications.description: Enable notifications and choose which paths should create Event entities. All notifications are sent to Home Assistant as events.

data.notification_paths: Notification paths to create event entities for (one per line, empty to disable)
data.notification_ignore_prefixes: Notification prefixes to ignore for event entities (one per line)

auth.title: Signal K Authorization
auth.description: This Signal K server requires approval. Open {approval_url} (or the Signal K admin UI) and approve the access request. Home Assistant continues automatically once approved.

override_host.title: Signal K reports a different address
override_host.description: You entered {entered}, but the Signal K server reports its own address as {discovered}. If Home Assistant cannot resolve the reported address (common when both run in Docker and the server uses a .local mDNS name), keep this option enabled to use the address you entered. Disable it to trust the server-reported address.

progress.auth: Waiting for approval. Open {approval_url} (or the Signal K admin UI) and approve the access request.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check the host, port, and TLS settings.
error.cannot_resolve: Could not resolve the host. If the address ends in .local (mDNS), Home Assistant running in Docker often cannot resolve it. Try the server's IP address instead, or run Home Assistant with host networking.
error.connection_timeout: Connection timed out. The address may be reachable but the Signal K server did not respond within 5 seconds.
error.discovery_failed: Signal K discovery did not return endpoints.
error.auth_required: This Signal K server requires credentials before access requests can be created.
error.auth_not_supported: Authentication is required but access requests are not supported.
error.auth_failed: Authentication failed. Approve the request and try again.
